questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to be close to Copenhagen, but still be somewhere to explore a new and different city. I also wanted a place where I was more financial flexible where it wasn't important to get grands. Another crucial aspect was that it was a beautiful city, where it is safe and there is a really good study environment with a lot of students from all over the world.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay, I was a bit confused at some points, but there is a great communication system so you can write mails and call if you need more information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: In regards to school I received mails in regards to where to meet up and at what time I have to be places. Upon arriving we also had a zoom call if we had any questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it very difficult to find housing but there are a lot of different sides on Facebook where you can find a lot of opportunities or write to people that have just been on exchange.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is more expensive than campus and in Prague there are a lot of Airbnb etc. that are really expensive so you have to be a bit critical. Though I would say that off campus you can choose to live closer to the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to go to the office for international students and bring a printed paper to get signed but it was easy and you can see that they are experienced. I also got a mail to be registered with a student id, which is very easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could call and write to the Erasmus office

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was a system I haven't experienced with using SIS but we had a zoom call where we saw how we registered to courses and there is a video on their official website. You had to be quick to apply for the courses you wanted and then you either got it or got waitlisted, they there are tryouts but I would say that you most of the time will get the courses you want, and if there is a course you are really interested in you can write to the teacher.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: hmm maybe I would say that there is nothing wrong with calling or writing the host if you are cunfused in any way.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I would say that it depends of what courses you choose and how you want to study abroad. I choose a mix of courses that was more fun and some that are more advanced which was more the MA classes, but I would say that as a BA student it wasn't hard taking a MA class.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Their teaching method is different for instance they count absences, there is more small papers through out the course and presentations, so for me the teaching method was more align with how it was I high school.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Dressing up Oneself and the Society: Fashion in the 19th and 20th Century Aesthetic
Menstruation and Contemporary Society: Theory, Research, Activism
Sociology of body
Balkan cinema
Global anthropology, decolonial theory

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Menstruation and Contemporary Society: Theory, Research, Activism 
Sociology of body
Global anthropology, decolonial theory (really great teacher, more like the teaching in CPH, it was a really interesting course so I would really recommend) 
You have more courses here because there it is less ECTS pr. course, so I would also recommend a movie course to get a little break from a lot of readings etc.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: i was pretty prepared so I dont think there were any unexpected costs, the only thing was you could buy a student card to get discount on different things but you could chose not to.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: housing was definitely more expensive than expected, their coffee is not that cheap as well, but cheaper than CPH

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: there were a lot of different thing available and you could be in a WhatsApp group where there were different opportunities, for instance hiking, exploring other cities, the opera, clubs and much more.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: eating out !! It is cheap and you can find a lot og different cousines. They have really good thrift shops and great cafes and bars as well as just walking around in the city with all the beautiful buildings etc.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: walking around the city, going to the museums and go down by the river and the castle, it is vey beautiful.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, it wasnt that different from my own culture, the only thing that was difficult is the communication because it is not everybody that can speak English.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I would say, just be open and a good starter is to ask if they know any nice areas or bars/cafes. people are usually really nice and friendly and want to help.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didnt experience any challenges in this.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Im not sure, I would say the friendliness and there is always a lot of people at bars so there is always a really good atmosphere.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't pack to much if you like thrifting! 
 don’t hesitate to reach out, especially to other international students people are really friendly 
I would say find a good balance between studying and free time and then maybe go to some beautiful hiking places outside of Prague or go to some small cities close.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: maybe just that I would say it is important to create a balance between school and exploring the city and its culture.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I meet abroad has been amazing, I would also say the cheap beers and cozy cafes and bars. They have a lot of outside areas and yards that are really nice to sit in, and it is nice to follow some different websites, facebook or instagram sites to see if there are any events in the following weekends. Then I would say that it has been nice with a break from UCPH in regards to choosing courses, because they are smaller the courses are also more narrow so you can choose a very specific topic to study.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I would say missing the people back home, sometimes it can be overwhelming so just remember that it is okay to relax as well and take a break from the social life.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
